title: Adding issued CRW forecasts cut 12-week global Alert extent MSE by 16.7% in a frozen 2023-2025 test
abstract: We tested whether biased CRW forecasts add useful information about global weekly Alert 1+ extent beyond season and current extent. We fitted linear models on 171 target weeks in 2019-2022 and froze them for 157 matched weeks in 2023-2025. At lead 12 weeks, adding the issued forecast aggregate cut MSE by 16.7%. A paired 13-week block 95% interval was 4.0% to 26.3%; a 26-week interval was 0.2% to 27.0%. The 99% intervals include zero. A three-harmonic seasonal control gave 11.1% reduction with an interval that includes zero. The gain was largest in 2024; 2023 gave a small loss. Mean extent rose from 2.77% in training to 7.61% in testing. The frozen full model still had -3.95 percentage points of mean error, while the raw aggregate had +10.80 points. The test supports possible useful aggregate information despite calibration error, but not stable skill across climate states or controls. It does not test biological bleaching, local risk or error causes. Code, attributed source aggregates, predictions, fits, audits and a figure permit reproduction without external downloads.
